Student-t latent errors

Source: R/errors.R
psp_t.Rd

Replaces the normal errors \(\varepsilon_{it} \sim N(0, 1)\) of psprobit() / psoprobit() by Student-t errors with df degrees of freedom, which makes the model robust to outlying observations (for binary outcomes this is the robit model of Liu 2004; df = 7 approximates the logit link). The errors are sampled as the scale mixture \(\varepsilon_{it} \sim N(0, v_{it})\), \(v_{it} \sim IG(\nu/2, \nu/2)\); the posterior means of \(v_{it}\) are returned in fit$v_mean (large values flag observations the model fits poorly).

Usage

psp_t(df = 7)

Arguments

df

Degrees of freedom, larger than 2.

Value

An object of class psp_errors.

Details

The degrees of freedom are fixed rather than estimated: with discrete outcomes the data carry very little information about them.

With t errors the latent outcome is no longer normal, because the spatial filter mixes the errors of several units. Probabilities and impacts are therefore averaged over control$mixture_draws simulated sets of \(v\) (fixed per fit, so results are reproducible): given \(v\) the latent outcome is normal and the usual formulas apply. Above impacts_exact_max units the reduced-form variance treats the own error term exactly and the neighbours' terms at their mean.

References

Liu, C. (2004). Robit regression: a simple robust alternative to logistic and probit regression. In Gelman, A. and Meng, X.-L. (eds.), Applied Bayesian Modeling and Causal Inference from Incomplete-Data Perspectives, 227-238. Wiley.

Examples

W <- psp_weights(rook_weights(5, 5), style = "W")
d <- sim_psprobit(W, T = 4, beta = c(0, 1, -1), rho = 0.4, df = 5, seed = 1)
fit <- psprobit(y ~ x1 + x2, d, c("id", "time"), W, errors = psp_t(df = 5),
                impacts = FALSE,
                control = psp_control(iter = 300, warmup = 200, chains = 1, seed = 1))
#> Warning: Possible convergence problems (R-hat > 1.01 or bulk ESS < 100) for: (Intercept), x1, x2, rho, sigma_alpha. Consider more iterations.
coef(fit)
#> (Intercept)          x1          x2         rho sigma_alpha 
#>   0.1290682   1.3537639  -1.1033764   0.3442226   1.5044671
